{{short description|German physicist (1935–1994)}}
'''Jens Scheer''' (30 May 1935 – 18 July 1994), was a [[physicist]], professor of [[nuclear physics]] at the [[University of Bremen]] and one of Germany's best-known [[Anti-nuclear movement|anti-nuclear activists]].

Scheer was a member of the Communist Party of Germany (KPD). For reason of his KPD-membership and his political activities, Scheer was threatened in 1975 with the loss of his academic position at the University of Bremen and an interdiction of enacting his profession, as membership in the KPD and his position as university professor were considered incompatible. The legal proceedings lasted for about five years, after which the final verdict was the payment of a fine.<ref>[[Brian Martin (social scientist)|Brian Martin]]: [http://www.uow.edu.au/~bmartin/pubs/86spp.html ''Nuclear suppression''], section "Federal Republic of Germany". Also published in Science and Public Policy, vol.&nbsp;13, no.&nbsp;6, December 1986, pp.&nbsp;312-320</ref>

One of Scheer's main research interests was low-level radiation and its effects on human beings. He claimed that radiation exposure at critical moments in life weakens the immune system, thus leading to a higher susceptibility to infectious diseases. After the [[Chernobyl disaster]] of 1986, he invested considerable efforts in attempting to determine the extent of damage caused in the longer term by this disaster.

In an article, Scheer claimed that low-level radiation had caused the death of millions, when all direct and indirect effects of radiation are taken together. His view was criticized as unfounded.<ref>J. Scheer: ''Tödliche Täuschung: Radioaktive Niedrigstrahlung hat den Tod von vielen Millionen Menschen verursacht'', cited and discussed in: Kultur & Technik, 2/1991, Deutsches Museum, [http://www.deutsches-museum.de/fileadmin/Content/data/Insel/Information/KT/heftarchiv/1991/15-2-9.pdf#page=3 p. 11 ff.]</ref>

Scheer also published on several stochastic models proposed in the context of quantum theory, in particular those advanced by [[Jean-Pierre Vigier]] and by J.C. Aron, and he criticized a prevalence of [[positivism]] in quantum physics.<ref>Jens Scheer: ''Gegen die Kopenhagener Deutung der Quantentheorie'' ("Against the Copenhague interpretation of quantum mechanics"), interview with Jens Scheer by Klaus v. Bloh, held in June/July 1994, [http://www.streitbarer-materialismus.de/ Streitbarer Materialismus], no.&nbsp;20 (in German language)</ref>

In 1994, Scheer died of heart failure.<ref>[http://www.nadir.org/nadir/initiativ/maus-bremen/Arbeitsschwerpunkte/arch61.html Obituary Jens Scheer], University of Bremen, downloaded 27. November 2011</ref>

'''Articles relating to low-level radiation and Chernobyl'''
* Jens Scheer: [http://www.bmj.com/highwire/filestream/308942/field_highwire_article_pdf/0/843.3.full.pdf ''Neonatal mortality in Germany since the Chernobyl explosion''], British Medical Journal [http://www.bmj.com/content/304/6830/843.3.full.pdf 1992;304:843.3], Letter, March 1992, {{doi|10.1136/bmj.304.6830.843-b}}
* Jens Scheer: [http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v326/n6112/abs/326449b0.html ''How many Chernobyl fatalities?''], Scientific Correspondence, ''Nature'' 326, 449, April 1987, {{doi|10.1038/326449b0}}

'''Articles and book chapters on quantum physics'''
* Jens Scheer: [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF00666026 ''A view of EPR non-locality problems based on Aron's stochastic foundation of relativity''], Foundations of Physics Letters, vol.&nbsp;3, no.&nbsp;6, pp.&nbsp;577–580, 1990, {{doi|10.1007/BF00666026}}
* Jens Scheer, Klaus Götsch, Thomas Koch, Günter Lüning, Michael Schmidt, Heiko Ziggel: [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF00690080 ''A possible evidence for a violation of Heisenberg's position-momentum uncertainty relation''], Foundations of Physics Letters, vol.&nbsp;2, no.&nbsp;1, pp.&nbsp;71–79, 1989, {{doi|10.1007/BF00690080}}
* Jens Scheer, Michael Schmidt: ''Remarks on EPR-related concepts from a realistic point of view'', In [[Alwyn Van der Merwe]], [[Franco Selleri]], G.
